title: Windows CI: run clippy and the whole test suite, and launch the installed app
body:
Part of porting Ivy to Windows entirely (Linux and macOS already work). Found by the Windows porting inventory.

## What is wrong

- `.github/workflows/ivy-prerelease.yml:22-37`: clippy and `cargo test` run on `ubuntu-24.04` only.
- The `windows` job (`:192-225`) only runs `cargo build --release ... --bins` and the installer lifecycle.
- `packaging/windows/test-install.ps1` never starts `Ivy.exe` and sets `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` itself (`:11`), which hides A2.
- `#[cfg(windows)]` test arms (`endpoint.rs:363`, `metadata.rs:425`, `client.rs:449`, `splitting.rs:466`) have never compiled.
- **Effect:** the published installer crashed on launch, and nothing caught it.
- The suite is pervasively `sh`-based: `Pty::spawn("sh", ["-c", ...])` throughout `pty_output.rs`, `lib.rs`, `resume.rs` and others. A Windows `cargo test` will fail wholesale until tests are gated or given a `cmd`/`pwsh` arm.
- **Fix:**
  - Add a `windows-2025` job: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo test --workspace`. Gate Unix-shell tests behind `cfg(unix)` with a reported skip count, never silent (see the F2.7 row about early-returning tests).
  - Add a launch smoke test. Start `Ivy.exe` with a clean profile (no `XDG_*`, no `SHELL`) and a measuring or self-closing mode (`measure.rs` already has one). Assert it opens a console, writes its layout under `%APPDATA%`, and exits 0.

## Acceptance criteria

- A regression like the current launch crash fails CI.
  - Every `#[cfg(windows)]` test arm compiles and runs.
  - Skipped Unix-only tests are counted in the job output, never silent.

## Depends on

- #161
